name: No Kick Drum
description: Generate a pattern without any kick drum or low-frequency impact sounds. The low end must be carried by bass, drone, or textural elements.
usefulWhen: Forcing creativity in the low end, breaking reliance on the kick as a structural element
repair: Ensure something provides low-frequency weight — a sub drone, filtered noise, or bass tone. No low end at all feels thin rather than creative.
strudelHints: Replace kick with: low sine note every 4 cycles, filtered noise pulse, or metallic resonance with long decay

name: Only Sine Waves
description: Every sound source must be a sine wave. No samples, no complex waveforms, no noise. Pure sinusoidal tones only.
usefulWhen: Exploring the essence of tone, creating extreme purity, focusing on frequency relationships and beating patterns
repair: Use multiple sine layers at different frequencies and gain levels. FM between sine waves for more complex timbres. The purity is the point.
strudelHints: All sounds: s('sine'). Use note() for pitch.
Layer 5-8 sine waves at different frequencies for a harmonic series drone
Beat frequencies between close sine tones create rhythm without percussion

name: Maximum 3 Sounds
description: The entire pattern uses at most 3 distinct sound sources. Every layer must derive from one of these 3 sounds.
usefulWhen: Forcing depth over breadth — make 3 sounds rich and evolving rather than 8 sounds thin and static
repair: Each of the 3 sounds must do heavy lifting through processing. Use filtering, reverb, gain modulation, and layering to create variety from limited sources.
strudelHints: Count distinct s() calls — maximum 3 different sample/sound names
Use different .lpf(), .room(), .gain() settings on copies of the same source to create distinct layers

name: Silence as Primary Element
description: More than 50% of the pattern duration must be silence or near-silence (gain < 0.05 on all layers). Sound events are rare and significant.
usefulWhen: Creating extreme tension, making every sound event meaningful, exploring the edge of audibility
repair: The few events that do occur must be carefully chosen and placed. Each one should feel significant. Use long reverbs so the space between events has content (decay tails).
strudelHints: Long .room(0.95) reverb tails fill the silence
One event every 8-16 cycles, gaining significance through rarity
